## Anesthesia, Drug and Fluid Administration

Administration of anesthetics, sedatives, analgesics, antibiotics, anti-inflammatories, fluids and other substances to a subject, whether as clinical care or as the experimental treatment.

### Analgesic

The administration of a pain-relieving agent, such as buprenorphine or meloxicam. Use this for systemic analgesia given before, during, or after a potentially painful intervention.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Volume administered` | Quantity with unit. Total volume of solution delivered to the animal in this administration, not the share of any one component. Units: mL, µL, L. |
| `Administration route` | **Required.** Choice. Route of analgesic administration. Options: Subcutaneous (SC), Intraperitoneal (IP), Intramuscular (IM), Intravenous (IV), Oral, Topical, Other. |
| `Indication` | Choice. Whether the analgesic was given to prevent expected pain or to treat pain already present. Options: Prophylactic, Therapeutic. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

### Anesthesia

The administration of anesthetic agents to induce unconsciousness, analgesia, or sedation. This entry captures anesthetic protocol details and can stand alone or support a larger procedure episode.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Anesthetic depth` | Choice. The anesthetic depth reached; deep sedation is not surgical plane. Options: Light sedation, Moderate sedation, Deep sedation, Surgical plane, Other. |
| `End of anesthesia` | Text. Time when anesthesia ended, as HH:MM. |
| `Total duration` | Quantity with unit. Total time the animal spent under anesthesia, across every phase of it. Units: h, min, s. |
| `Recovery time` | Quantity with unit. Time from end of anesthesia to return of righting reflex or normal activity. Units: h, min, s. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |
| `Monitoring` | Table of rows. What was followed during the anesthetic, how it was assessed, and how often. One row per parameter; an empty table means nothing was monitored. |
| `Monitoring › Parameter` | **Required.** Choice. What this row followed — the parameter itself, never the instrument that read it. Anesthetic depth is one of them: choose it, and record the checks used beside it. Options: Anesthetic depth, Blood pressure, Heart rate, Oxygen saturation, Respiratory rate, Temperature, Other. |
| `Monitoring › Assessment method` | Multi-select. How this parameter was assessed; select every check or instrument used. Options: Pedal withdrawal (toe pinch), Palpebral reflex, Corneal reflex, Tail pinch, Visual observation, Pulse oximetry, ECG, EEG, Capnography, Rectal probe, Other. |
| `Monitoring › Interval` | Quantity with unit. How often this parameter was checked. Leave empty for continuous monitoring. Units: h, min, s. |
| `Supportive care` | Table of rows. Care given alongside the anesthetic. One row per measure; an empty table means none was given. |
| `Supportive care › Measure` | **Required.** Choice. Which supportive measure was given while the animal was under. Options: Eye lubricant, Fluid therapy, Heating pad, Oxygen supplementation, Other. |

| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

### Drug administration (other)

Use this catch-all only for medication that does not fit a dedicated type, such as a hormone, reversal agent, antidote, or supplement. File by why the drug was given, not by what the drug is: meloxicam for pain is an analgesic, not a drug administration.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Purpose` | **Required.** Choice. What the substance was given for. Use a dedicated procedure type wherever one fits. Options: Hormone, Reversal / antidote, Supplement, Other. |
| `Administration role` | Choice. Whether the substance was given as supportive care or as the experimental treatment itself. Options: Clinical care, Experimental treatment. |
| `Volume administered` | Quantity with unit. Total volume of solution delivered to the animal in this administration. Units: mL, µL, L. |
| `Administration route` | **Required.** Choice. Route of administration. Options: Subcutaneous (SC), Intraperitoneal (IP), Intramuscular (IM), Intravenous (IV), Oral, Topical, Inhaled, Other. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

### Fluid therapy

The administration of a physiological solution, such as saline or Ringer's solution, for hydration or volume support. Record the total procedure-level volume and the clinical problem it addressed; state the delivery profile rather than leaving the rate empty to imply a bolus.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Total volume administered` | **Required.** Quantity with unit. Total volume of fluid administered in this event, summed across every site. Units: L, mL, µL. |
| `Administration route` | **Required.** Choice. Route of fluid administration. Options: Subcutaneous (SC), Intraperitoneal (IP), Intravenous (IV), Intraosseous (IO), Oral, Other. |
| `Delivery profile` | Choice. The shape the delivery took over time. Options: Bolus injection, Slow injection, Continuous infusion. |
| `Infusion rate` | Quantity with unit. The rate set for this delivery, as configured rather than measured afterwards. Units: mL/h, mL/kg/h, µL/h. |
| `Number of sites` | Integer. How many separate needle placements or entry points the total volume was divided across. Range: ≥ 1. |
| `Fluid temperature` | Quantity with unit. Temperature of the fluid itself when it was given, not the animal's body temperature. Units: °C, °F, K. |
| `Fluid indication` | Choice. Which clinical problem the fluid was given to address. Options: Dehydration, Perioperative support, Blood or fluid loss, Reduced intake or anorexia, Hypoglycaemia, Other. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

### Local anesthetic

A site-directed nerve block, infiltration, or topical application, such as bupivacaine at an incision line. Use Analgesic instead for systemic pain relief.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Volume administered` | Quantity with unit. Total volume of anaesthetic solution placed at the site in this administration. Units: mL, µL, L. |
| `Placement technique` | **Required.** Choice. How the anaesthetic was physically deposited in or on the tissue. Options: Infiltration, Perineural injection, Splash / bathing, Instillation, Topical application, Other. |
| `Site` | Text. Structure or region the anaesthetic was placed at; record the side in the laterality field. |
| `Laterality` | Choice. Which side of the body the anaesthetic was placed on. Options: Left, Right, Bilateral, Midline. |
| `Guidance method` | Choice. How the target was located while the anaesthetic was being placed. Options: Blind / landmark, Nerve locator, Ultrasound, Direct vision, Other. |
| `Application dwell time` | Quantity with unit. How long a topical preparation was left in contact before the next step: the wait after applying, not how long the delivery took. Units: s, min, h. |
| `Block effectiveness` | Choice. The operator's judgement of whether the block worked, from the response seen at the first incision. Options: No response at incision, Reduced response, Full response, Not assessed. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

### Sedative

A sedative or anxiolytic given for non-surgical restraint, imaging, or transport, as distinct from full anesthesia. Record the level the animal actually reached, which may be deeper than the level intended.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Volume administered` | Quantity with unit. Total volume of solution that entered the animal in this event, vehicle included. Units: mL, µL, L. |
| `Infusion rate` | Quantity with unit. Rate the sedative infusion ran at; the delivery profile says whether there was one. Units: mL/h, µL/h. |
| `Administration route` | **Required.** Choice. Route of sedative administration. Options: Subcutaneous (SC), Intraperitoneal (IP), Intramuscular (IM), Intravenous (IV), Inhaled, Oral, Other. |
| `Delivery profile` | Choice. Shape the delivery took over time, which an empty rate cannot state. Options: Bolus injection, Slow injection, Continuous infusion. |
| `Sedation level` | Choice. The level the animal actually reached; deep sedation is not surgical plane. Options: Light sedation, Moderate sedation, Deep sedation, Surgical plane, Other. |
| `Sedation duration` | Quantity with unit. Time from administration of the agent to the end of the sedation. Units: h, min, s. |
| `Recovery time` | Quantity with unit. Time from the end of the sedation until the animal rights itself and moves normally. Units: h, min, s. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |
| `Monitoring` | Table of rows. What was followed while the animal was sedated, how, and how often. One row per parameter; an empty table means nothing was monitored. |
| `Monitoring › Parameter` | **Required.** Choice. What this row followed — the parameter itself, never the instrument that read it. Anesthetic depth covers the sedation level. Options: Anesthetic depth, Blood pressure, Heart rate, Oxygen saturation, Respiratory rate, Temperature, Other. |
| `Monitoring › Assessment method` | Multi-select. How this parameter was assessed; select every check or instrument used. Options: Pedal withdrawal (toe pinch), Palpebral reflex, Corneal reflex, Tail pinch, Visual observation, Pulse oximetry, ECG, EEG, Capnography, Rectal probe, Other. |
| `Monitoring › Interval` | Quantity with unit. How often this parameter was checked. Leave empty for continuous monitoring. Units: h, min, s. |
| `Supportive care` | Table of rows. Care given alongside the sedation. One row per measure; an empty table means none was given. |
| `Supportive care › Measure` | **Required.** Choice. Which supportive measure was given while the animal was sedated. Options: Eye lubricant, Fluid therapy, Heating pad, Oxygen supplementation, Other. |

## Surgical Procedures

Surgical steps on the skull and head, such as burr holes, craniotomies, cranial windows, head fixation, headposts, headcaps and baseplating.

### Baseplating

Documents fixing a baseplate to the skull or headcap to dock a head-mounted miniature microscope, typically over a previously implanted GRIN lens or prism.

This type has no type-specific fields. The record's own fields and its material rows describe it.

### Burr hole

A small hole drilled in the skull to provide access for electrode placement, cannula insertion, injection, or another targeted action while otherwise maintaining skull integrity.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Hole diameter` | Quantity with unit. Diameter of the burr hole. Units: mm, µm, cm, m. |
| `Drill speed` | Quantity with unit. Speed of the drill. Units: RPM, Hz. |
| `Purpose` | Text. Primary purpose of creating the burr hole. |
| `Cooling method` | Choice. Method used to prevent overheating during drilling. Options: Saline irrigation, Air cooling, None, Other. |
| `Dura handling` | Choice. How the dura was left by this opening; an incidental nick counts as punctured. Options: Left intact, Punctured, Incised, Excised. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

### Cranial window

A section of skull opened and fitted with a transparent window for direct, often long-term optical access to the brain surface.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Surgical method` | Text. Describe the surgical technique used to create the cranial window. Common methods include the use of a surgical drill, bone saw, automatic or manual cutting tools to remove a section of the skull. |
| `Shape of cranial window` | Text. Describe the shape of the cranial window performed, such as square, circular, elliptical, or other specific form. This helps in understanding the surgical approach and potential impact on the underlying brain tissue. |
| `Dimensions of cranial window` | Text. Dimensions of the window: length, width, diameter or thickness. E.g., '1.0 mm diameter × 4 mm length'. |
| `Orientation of cranial window` | Text. Describe the orientation of the cranial window relative to anatomical landmarks. This can include angle and direction, which are important for precise targeting and minimizing damage to critical areas. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

### Craniectomy

Removal of a portion of the skull that is left open: the bone is not replaced and the opening is not sealed again. Use Craniotomy when the opening is closed afterwards.

|:------|:------------|
| `Surgical method` | Text. Describe the surgical technique used for the craniectomy. Common methods include the use of a surgical drill, bone saw, automatic or manual cutting tools to remove a section of the skull. |
| `Shape of craniectomy` | Text. Describe the shape of the craniectomy, such as square, circular, oval, or irregular. |
| `Dimensions of craniectomy` | Text. Dimensions of the craniectomy: length, width, or diameter. E.g., '1.0 mm diameter × 4 mm length'. |
| `Orientation of craniectomy` | Text. Indicate the orientation of the craniectomy relative to major anatomical landmarks. |
| `Dura handling` | Choice. How the dura was left by this opening; an incidental nick counts as punctured. Options: Left intact, Punctured, Incised, Excised. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

| `Vascular access route` | Choice. Where the perfusate entered the circulation. Options: Intracardiac (transcardial), Carotid, Intra-aortic, Intracranial, Other. |
| `Perfusion scope` | Choice. How far the perfusate was carried through the animal. Options: Whole body, Head only, Other. |
| `Perfusion drive` | Choice. What pushed the perfusate through the circulation. Options: Gravity feed, Peristaltic pump, Syringe pump, Pressurized line, Manual syringe, Other. |
| `Perfusion pressure` | Quantity with unit. Pressure the perfusate was delivered at, read from the regulator or the height of the reservoir. Units: mmHg, cmH₂O, kPa. |
| `Heart beating at start` | Yes/no. Check this if the heart was still beating when the perfusate first entered the circulation. |
| `Perfusion phases` | Table of rows. Each phase of the perfusion, one row per phase, in the order they were delivered. The wash and the fixative make different claims about volume, rate, duration, and temperature, so each states its own. |
| `Perfusion phases › Phase` | **Required.** Choice. What this row delivered: the wash that clears blood from the circulation (a rinse and a flush are the same step under one name), the fixative that follows it, or another step. Options: Wash, Fixative, Other. |
| `Perfusion phases › Volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume delivered in this phase, as it was actually run rather than as planned. Units: L, mL, µL, nL, pL. |
| `Perfusion phases › Rate` | Quantity with unit. Rate at which this phase's solution moved through the circulation. Units: L/min, mL/min, µL/min. |
| `Perfusion phases › Duration` | Quantity with unit. How long this phase ran. Fixative contact time is what over- and under-fixation are compared on, and it is normally not the same as the wash duration. Units: h, min, s. |
| `Perfusion phases › Temperature` | Quantity with unit. Temperature of the solution delivered in this phase. Units: °C. |
| `Signs of completion` | Multi-select. Which conventional signs that the perfusion was working were actually seen. Options: Liver blanching, Clear effluent, Fixation tremor, Tissue rigidity, Pale brain. |
| `Failure modes` | Multi-select. What went wrong, if anything; tick every fault that applied. Leave empty if nothing went wrong. Options: Clotting, Cannula misplaced, Atrium not opened, Oedema, Circuit leak, Air embolism, Residual blood, Other. |
| `Confirmation of death` | Multi-select. How death was verified at the end of the perfusion. Tick every check that was made; verification normally combines more than one. Options: Absence of heartbeat, Absence of breathing, Absence of reflexes, Fixed dilated pupils, Loss of corneal reflex, Other. |
| `Fatal outcome` | Choice. Whether the animal died with this procedure, and whether that was intended; record it only on the procedure that actually ended the animal. Options: Not fatal, Planned terminal, Unintended death. |

## Endpoint Procedures (Euthanasia)

Methods used to euthanize a subject, such as barbiturate or inhalant overdose, CO₂ exposure, cervical dislocation and decapitation.

### Barbiturate injection

Euthanasia by administration of a barbiturate solution using an appropriate route.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Concentration` | Quantity with unit. Concentration of the barbiturate solution. Units: mg/mL, µg/mL, g/L, mg/L, µg/L. |
| `Dosage` | Quantity with unit. Dosage administered per kilogram of body weight. Units: mg/kg, µg/kg, g/kg. |
| `Administration route` | **Required.** Choice. Route of barbiturate administration. Options: Intraperitoneal (IP), Intravenous (IV), Intracardiac, Subcutaneous (SC), Other. |
| `Volume administered` | Quantity with unit. Total volume of barbiturate solution administered. Units: mL, L, µL, nL. |
| `Time to unconsciousness` | Quantity with unit. Observed time to loss of consciousness. Units: s, min, h, ms. |
| `Confirmation of death` | **Required.** Multi-select. Methods used to confirm death. Options: Absence of heartbeat, Absence of breathing, Absence of reflexes, Fixed dilated pupils, Loss of corneal reflex, Additional dose administered, Other. |

### CO₂ chamber euthanasia

Euthanasia using controlled exposure to carbon dioxide in a chamber.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `CO₂ concentration` | **Required.** Quantity with unit. Concentration of CO₂ used in the chamber. Units: %, ppm, ppb. |
| `CO₂ Flow Rate` | Quantity with unit. Rate of CO₂ flow into the chamber. Units: L/min, mL/min, L/s, mL/s. |
| `Exposure Duration` | **Required.** Quantity with unit. Duration of CO₂ exposure. Units: s, min, h, ms. |
| `Time to unconsciousness` | Quantity with unit. Observed time to loss of consciousness. Units: s, min, h, ms. |
| `Chamber prefilling` | Choice. Method of chamber prefilling with CO₂. Options: Not prefilled, Partially prefilled, Fully prefilled, Other. |
| `Chamber volume` | Quantity with unit. Volume of the euthanasia chamber. Units: L, mL, µL. |
| `Gradual CO₂ introduction` | Yes/no. Check if CO₂ was introduced gradually (recommended for animal welfare). |
| `Confirmation of death` | **Required.** Multi-select. Methods used to confirm death. Options: Absence of heartbeat, Absence of breathing, Absence of reflexes, Fixed dilated pupils, Loss of corneal reflex, Continued CO₂ exposure, Other. |
